channel.title: Apsis — Blog
channel.description: Field notes from Apsides Labs on AI, engineering and intelligent learning systems.

item.title: When AI agents don't stay in their lane
item.description: Anthropic pulled live internet access from its internal evaluations after its agents exploited real websites. What happened, and what every builder of autonomous systems should take from it.

item.title: The week AI agents became coworkers
item.description: Microsoft bills agents by usage, OpenAI ships always-on dots, and Anthropic cuts prices. The shift from assistants to workers is now a budgeting, permissions and accountability problem.

item.title: Capable AI on CPU-only, constrained hosts
item.description: You don't need a GPU cluster to run useful models. How we ship voice and language models on CPU-only, constrained hosts.

item.title: Why offline-first learning still matters
item.description: Most of the world's learners are not on a fast, always-on connection. Designing for the lowest common denominator makes learning software better for everyone.

item.title: Why CPU-only AI is the right default for learning software
item.description: GPUs are fast and expensive. For the software most learners actually use, a small model on a CPU is the better trade.

item.title: Building a dictionary for a language the web ignores
item.description: 348 words, one static page, no backend. What it takes to give a low-resource language a real learning tool.

item.title: Static sites outlive their frameworks
item.description: We ship plain HTML that runs anywhere and needs no build. Here is why that is a feature, not nostalgia.

item.title: Evaluating small models honestly
item.description: Published benchmarks will not tell you whether a 1B model is good enough for your task. A short, practical method that will.

item.title: Teaching a script, not just a language
item.description: Learning Assamese or Bodo means learning a script. What we changed after watching people try.
